reuse.why: The new handler reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment, while budget iteration now uses the existing getNextDateAfter helper.

duplication.why: Daily skipping, holiday matching and date shifting remain centralized, and repeated budget adjustment logic is removed.

placement.why: Calendar rules live in shared schedules utilities, configuration belongs in RecurConfig, and handler orchestration stays in the server schedules module.

scope.why: The changes are confined to the requested scheduling rules, range handler, supporting consumers and tests.

maintainability.why: The shared implementation is straightforward, although getDateWithSkippedWeekend now understates its holiday and occurrence-skipping responsibilities and accepts an unnecessarily broad string frequency.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Both server date handlers use the shared adjustment helper, and budget iteration delegates to shared next-date helpers.

disguised_duplication.where: Holiday matching and daily-versus-other-frequency handling are shared rather than reproduced through renamed implementations.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains frequency and holidays parameters and a daily-frequency branch; these represent requested domain variations, and consumers continue using the helper.
